message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Westbridge's 2026–27 exam regulations (sections 4–11). Arrive 15 minutes early; if you are up to 30 minutes late the invigilator may let you in, without extra time, and later than that you're marked absent. No one may leave in the first 30 or last 15 minutes, and toilet trips are escorted. Show your student ID on the desk; without it you'll be admitted but must verify your identity at the Examinations Office within 24 hours. Only pens, pencils, erasers, rulers and an unlabelled clear water bottle are allowed. Calculators are allowed only if the paper permits them and only approved Casio fx-83GT/fx-85GT models. Phones and smart watches may be kept on your person provided they are switched off; using one is an offence. If illness or other circumstances stop you sitting an exam or seriously affect it, submit a mitigating circumstances claim with independent evidence within five working days; your module leader decides the claim. Sitting the exam means you declare yourself fit. Failed modules can be resat once in August, with the resit mark capped at 40%. Misconduct goes to the Academic Conduct Officer, with penalties from zero marks to expulsion. Provisional results appear on the portal, usually within 20 working days of the exam period ending.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
UNIVERSITY OF WESTBRIDGE — REGULATIONS FOR CANDIDATES IN UNIVERSITY EXAMINATIONS (2026–27), Sections 4–10

4. Attendance and late arrival. Candidates should arrive at the examination venue at least 15 minutes before the start time. A candidate who arrives up to 30 minutes after the start may be admitted at the invigilator's discretion but will not be given extra time. A candidate arriving more than 30 minutes after the start will not be admitted and will be recorded as absent.

5. Leaving the room. Candidates may not leave the examination room during the first 30 minutes or the last 15 minutes of the examination. Candidates who leave temporarily, for example to use the toilet, must be accompanied by an invigilator.

6. Identification. Candidates must display their student ID card on the desk throughout the examination. A candidate without ID will be admitted but must report to the Examinations Office within 24 hours to verify their identity.

7. Permitted and prohibited items. Only pens, pencils, erasers, rulers and a clear water bottle without a label are allowed on the desk. Calculators may be used only where the examination paper's front page states that they are permitted, and only models on the University's approved list (Casio fx-83GT and fx-85GT series). Mobile phones, smart watches and other electronic devices must be switched off and placed in your bag at the front of the room before the examination starts. Having a mobile phone or smart watch on your person during the examination is an offence under the Academic Misconduct Regulations, even if the device is switched off and not used.

8. Mitigating circumstances. If illness or other circumstances beyond your control prevent you from sitting an examination, or seriously affect your performance, you may submit a mitigating circumstances claim through the student portal no later than five working days after the examination, with independent supporting evidence. Claims are decided by the Faculty Mitigating Circumstances Panel. Module leaders, personal tutors and examiners do not decide claims and cannot promise any outcome. By sitting an examination, you are declaring yourself fit to do so.

9. Resits. A student who fails a module at the first attempt may resit it once. The module mark for a resit is capped at the pass mark of 40%. However, where a mitigating circumstances claim for the first attempt has been accepted by the Panel, the next attempt is treated as a first sitting and the mark is not capped. Resit examinations take place in the August resit period.

10. Academic misconduct. Suspected misconduct, including copying, communicating with other candidates, possessing unauthorised materials or devices, and impersonation, will be reported to the Academic Conduct Officer. Penalties range from a mark of zero for the examination to expulsion from the University.

11. Results. Provisional marks are released on the student portal after ratification by the Board of Examiners, normally within 20 working days of the end of the examination period.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. What is the latest I can arrive after the start and still possibly be let in?
2. Can I keep my switched-off smart watch on my wrist during the exam?
3. I submitted a mitigating circumstances claim for my statistics exam. Who will decide it?
4. I missed my first attempt through illness and my mitigating claim was accepted. If I score 65% in August, what mark will I get?
response:
Answers are taken from the regulations themselves. Two points in my earlier notes were wrong, and I've marked them below.

**1. Latest arrival:** Up to **30 minutes after the start**, and only if the invigilator agrees. You won't get extra time. If you arrive more than 30 minutes late you won't be let in and will be recorded as absent. You're expected to arrive at least 15 minutes before the start. (Section 4)

**2. Smart watch on your wrist:** **No.** *(My notes were wrong here.)* Phones, smart watches and other electronic devices must be switched off and put in your bag at the front of the room before the exam starts. Having one on your person during the exam is an offence under the Academic Misconduct Regulations, **even if it's switched off and not used**. Penalties can range from zero marks for the exam to expulsion. (Sections 7 and 10)

**3. Who decides your claim:** The **Faculty Mitigating Circumstances Panel**. *(My notes wrongly said the module leader.)* Module leaders, personal tutors and examiners don't decide claims and can't promise any outcome. Claims must be submitted through the student portal, with independent evidence, within five working days of the exam. (Section 8)

**4. Scoring 65% in August after an accepted claim:** You'd get **65%**. Because the Panel accepted your claim for the first attempt, the August sitting counts as a first sitting, so the 40% resit cap doesn't apply. My notes left out this exception. (Section 9)
